evidence.clarity: Headline 'A lamp that wakes you the way a window does.' is a metaphor; the lede ('Thirty minutes before you want to be up, Morrow starts to glow') and 'No app. No screen. One dial.' make what/for-whom clear. 'Reserve a place' plus the $20 line under it gives the next step at 1440.
evidence.fit: Gets a feel for the light (auto-playing scene and dial), labels drawings, avoids sleep claims, says 'Planned for autumn 2027. A plan, not a promise.' But the brief says checkout isn't connected and there is no backend, and the page's 'Hold my place' form claims 'Your place is held. We've noted me@test.com' while HOLD_ENDPOINT is empty and the address only goes to localStorage. The action does not match what the business can actually do today.
evidence.distinctiveness: The whole page scrolls from night (#1C2235) through an ember-to-dawn gradient into a paper 'morning' section, and the 'What the thirty minutes look like' list is drawn as colour bands for 0/5/15/25/30 min. You would know this page without the logo. The lamp scene and dial are custom.
evidence.proof: 1440: the lamp scene auto-plays the 18 s sunrise on load (6:30 to 7:00, status ends 'Full light, a warm white. Nothing rang.'), and the dial is in the first viewport. 390: scene and dial are on the first screen too. Captioned 'Drawn, not photographed.' The ramp section backs it up with a consistent colour sequence.
evidence.craft: Serif type is consistent and the spacing rhythm holds. At t=0 the 1440 hero scene is a near-black muddy rectangle until the autoplay brightens it. The '$20 refundable deposit, when deposits open' price line wraps awkwardly at 390, leaving 'open' alone on a line. Nav links are 25px-tall text with no visual weight.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow, and the dial is reachable by tap (tapping the right edge of the dial jumped to 6:55). But the first screen holds no reserve button: 'Reserve a place' sits at y=1009, below the hero copy. There is no menu, just three inline text links 24.5px tall ('Reserve' is 52x25), under the 44px target.
evidence.honesty: Hero discloses 'Deposits aren't open yet; you can hold a place with your email today', but submitting the form shows 'Your place is held... You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens' when nothing is sent anywhere. It also invents facts not in the brief: 'sits on a nightstand in Charlotte and has woken one of us every morning since spring', an automatic-refund-if-it-slips-a-season policy, a chime 'we're testing', and 'Questions we've been asked' for a company with no customers.
evidence.interaction: At all three widths: dial drag, tap, arrow, PageUp/Home/End and wheel all update the time, status and scene. Play/Pause/'Play it again' work. Form: empty and 'nope' show an inline error (the empty case says 'That doesn't look like an email address', which is slightly off). Valid entry shows the confirmation, which persists across reload, and 'That's the wrong address' restores the form. FAQ details open. No console errors. The success state is fake.
evidence.copy: Written in a calm voice with specific words ('A faint ember. You could sleep through this.', 'Nothing rang.', 'Hardware runs late.'). Buttons say what they do. 'What we can say, and what we can't' is plain. It loses points for invented specifics and a 'Questions we've been asked' heading the company cannot have earned.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the metaphor headline, the auto-playing lamp scene with dial, 'Reserve a place' and the deposit note are all in view, which is strong. 390: headline, scene and dial are in view but there is no action other than a 25px nav link, and the promise is a metaphor until the lede below the fold.

problems: 'Hold my place' reports 'Your place is held. We've noted <email>' and promises emails, but HOLD_ENDPOINT is '' and the address is only saved to localStorage, so the visitor believes they are in line when they are not

Invented facts presented as true (prototype 'in Charlotte' 'since spring', an automatic refund if the batch slips, a chime under test, 'Questions we've been asked'): exactly what a buyer burned by crowdfunding would distrust once found out
390: no reserve button in the first screen, and the only nav is three 25px-tall inline text links

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The primary conversion ('Reserve a place' leads to the 'Hold my place' form) reports success for something that did not happen. After submitting a valid email the page shows 'Your place is held. We've noted me@test.com. You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens, and another whenever the plan changes.' In the script, HOLD_ENDPOINT = '' so no request is made and the address is only written to localStorage('morrow.held'). Before submitting, the page says 'Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line' and never discloses that the email is not sent.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open A/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click 'Reserve a place' (scrolls to #reserve). Type me@test.com and click 'Hold my place'. The confirmation 'Your place is held...' appears. In DevTools Network no request is made; in Sources, line ~687 shows var HOLD_ENDPOINT = ''; Application > Local Storage shows morrow.held = me@test.com.

evidence.clarity: 'Wake to thirty minutes of sunrise. One dial, no app.' followed by 'Morrow is a bedside lamp. Turn the dial to the time you want to be up...' A stranger could repeat it. 'Reserve a Morrow' with '$20 deposit, refunded whenever you ask. Checkout isn't connected yet, so no card today.' directly under it.
evidence.fit: Each brief point is reflected: the sunrise simulator answers 'can't hold the lamp', 'Drawing of the prototype; not a photo' and 'Drawn from the current CAD', 'First batch planned for next autumn. We won't print a date', an explicit 'no sleep-science claims' aside, and a reserve action that opens a pre-filled email with the disclosure before the click. 'Settled / Still changing' speaks straight to a buyer burned by late hardware.
evidence.distinctiveness: The bedroom scene with the window that stays night while the lamp lights the room is product-specific, and so is the callout line drawing ('width: not final'). Otherwise the structure is familiar: two-column hero, numbered 4-step list, FAQ accordion, pricing panel card. Section colours step night > dawn > sand > morning, which is subtler than A's continuous ramp.
evidence.proof: 1440: the scene, dial, readout, Play button and part of the slider are in the first viewport. Play runs -30 to 0 in 15 s (at 5 s it read '-20 min Deep orange'), Pause shows 'Paused at -20 min.', and Resume and 'Play it again' work. Labelled 'Drawn, not measured: the colours here illustrate the thirty-minute rise.' At 390 the artifact starts at y=610, so the only artifact in the first screen is the scene top.
evidence.craft: The Lora/Carlito pairing is tidy and the type scale is consistent, with 44-54px buttons. Defect: the <figure class='sunrise'> keeps the browser's default 40px side margins, so at 390 the artifact is 278px wide and inset at x=56 while the text column starts at x=16. The readout ('Full brightness. This is the time you set.') wraps into a 4-line, ~100px column beside the dial.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow. Menu button opens the list, Escape closes it, and tapping 'The prototype' scrolls there and closes the menu. Targets are 44px or larger (range 44px tall, CTA 54px). First screen has the promise, CTA and disclosure. But the artifact is pushed below the fold and cramped by the figure margin, and the dial is 112px.
evidence.honesty: Every image is labelled where it appears ('Drawing of the prototype; not a photo.'). The CTA's real result is stated before the click ('Checkout isn't connected yet, so this opens an email to us... take nothing today'). No ship date, no sleep claims, a 'not a medical or sleep device' line. Minor issues: reserve@morrow.example is not a brief-supplied address, though it is a .example placeholder, and the 'Reserve one for $20' heading reads like a payment until the fine print.
evidence.interaction: Range slider (keyboard Home gives '-30 min Off', 12x ArrowRight gives '-18 min Deep orange'), dial drag at 1440 (to '-1 min') and tap at 390 (to '-5 min'), and Play/Pause/Resume/'Play it again' with a live note all update the scene, both the lamp-face and on-page dial pointers, and an aria-live phase. Menu toggles with aria-expanded and Escape. The mailto href is correct and pre-filled. No console errors. The dial itself is aria-hidden and keyboard goes through the slider, which is acceptable.
evidence.copy: Concrete and in the customer's world: 'Ten o'clock on a Sunday or six on a Monday; it is one turn either way. That sentence is the manual.', 'nothing glowing at three in the morning', 'A sound alarm takes one second. Morrow takes thirty minutes, on purpose.' Terms stay consistent. Some repetition of 'no app, no screen' across four sections.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise (thirty minutes of sunrise, one dial, no app), 'Reserve a Morrow' with the no-card disclosure, and the operable sunrise scene with dial, all in view. 390: promise, lede, CTA and disclosure are in view, but only the top of the scene image; nothing operable backs the promise until you scroll.

problems: 390: the sunrise artifact is below the first screen and squeezed to 278px by the figure's default 40px margins, leaving the phase readout as a narrow 4-line column beside the dial
Structure is a familiar template (two-column hero, numbered steps, pricing card, FAQ), and the colour-staged sections do less than the product could carry

Reserve goes to mailto:reserve@morrow.example, an address the brief never supplied (a .example placeholder). The 'Reserve one for $20' heading can read as a payment until the fine print under the button

reason: As a phone shopper burned by late crowdfunded hardware, B tells me exactly what happens before I tap (an email, no card, refund on request, a season rather than a date) and labels every drawing where it sits. A is the more beautiful and memorable page, but its 'Your place is held' confirmation is not true (nothing is sent) and it invents details like a Charlotte prototype and an auto-refund policy. As the founder, I would not put my name on that. If A's form honestly said it was not yet sent, or actually collected emails, and the invented specifics were cut, A's design would probably win.
